Confusion and Vertigo. Confusion of the head, with
the rising of the bitter fluid (fifth day), 1 .—Head confused and giddy when
retiring to bed at 10.30 (eleventh day), 1 .—Head weak and confused (twelfth
day), 1 .—Slight vertigo accompanying the rumbling and swelling in the
umbilical region (after six hours); increase of the vertigo, with straining
at stool (after seven hours and a half) ; vertigo, aggravated by even a
moderate warmth of the room (first day) ; an attack of vertigo, without
any exciting cause other than the Ptelea, so violent as to compel discon¬
tinuance of writing and to bow the head ou the hands, closing the eyes; it
was preceded and accompanied by mild nausea, with slight griping pains
in the stomach (after eight hours, second day), Ib .—Fits of vertigo, lasting
three to five minutes, relieved by moving about, but worse on sudden mo¬
tion ; sensation as if all objects about him were in quick violent agitation
(after two hours, second day) ; fits of vertigo not so frequent but more
decided; worse on sudden motion and bending forward (after four hours);
vertigo only when stooping (after six hours); vertigo all gone, but head
feels a little muddled (after seven hours, second day), 7 .—Vertigo, aggra¬
vated by even turning the head gradually (after half an hour), 10 .—Attempt¬
ing to walk aggravates the vertigo very much; unable to stand alone (after
forty-five minutes), 10 .—[60.] Vertigo, aggravated by rising from a chair

sudden giddiness and with faint feeling (after twenty minutes); too giddy
to sit up (after thirty-five minutes) ; rising aggravates the giddiness, 10 .—

head (second day), 1 *.—Ou rising, giddiness, with piercing pain through the
brain, accompanied by severe aching pain in the stomach (seventh day), 1 .

increase of abdominal tenderness (eighth day), 1 .—Giddiness, with the per¬
sistent nausea (tenth day), 1 .—The giddiness of head and reeling in walking
much increased (eleventh day), 1 .—L70.] Attacked with too much giddiness
and vertigo to keep up (twelfth day), 1 .—Giddiness (after second dose), 11 .—
Giddiness, dulness, and languor, in the afternoon (third day), 11 .— Head
in General. Head feels light (four hours and a half after fourth dose), 7a .
—Heaviness of the head, with a muddled feeling, and dull aching pain in
forehead (third day), 11 .—Sensation of fulness in brain (tenth day), 6 *.—

Teeth. Since the proving one of the right molar teeth of
lower jaw has commenced to decay, but whether the effect of the remedy
or not was uncertain, 6 '.—Teeth all ache and feel sore (after three hours,
third day), 4 '. — Aching of right molar teeth, lower jaw, at 7 p.m. (first
day), 6 '.—Toothache on rightside (fourteenth day), 6 *.—Aching of right molar
teeth, lower jaw, after going to bed (thirty-first and thirty-third days), 63 .
—From 4 to 8 p.m. aching of right molar teeth, commencing in lower
jaw and gradually extending to the upper of same side (fourth day), 6 .—
Aching of right molar teeth, lasting only a few minutes, at 2 p.m., return¬
ing at 6 p.m., lasting the remainder of the evening (fifth day), 6 .— [260.]
Pain in carious tooth, with extreme sensitiveness; soreness of the gums;
all the teeth feel sensitive, with a dull, aching pain, in the evening (fourth
day), 11 .—Teeth feel as if elongated (thirteenth day), 63 .—Sensation as if
food were lodged between the teeth on right side, commencing at lower
jaw, extending to upper (thirteenth day), 6 '.— Tongue. Yesterday the
tongue was slightly swollen, and had white fur on it; more of swelling and
fur to day, with burning of the mouth and lips, as if touched with tincture
of Aconite (fifth day), 10 '.—Tongue coated yellow and feeling rough (second
day), 4 '.—Tongue yellow, coated along the centre and base (third day), 4 '.—
Tongue coated yellow, and the papillse were red and prominent (sixth
night), 1 '.—Tongue coated yellowish, with red papillse (fifth day), lb .—Yel¬
low-coated tongue (fifth and thirty-first days), ,c .—Furred tongue (fourth and
fifth days), 3 .— [270.] The tongue, which had hitherto been clean, was coated
with a yellowish fur, and the nausea was persistent (sixth day), 1 .—Tongue
dry and coated light brown (second day), 1 '.—Tongue dry and coated brown¬
ish yellow (twelfth day), 1 .—Roughness of back part of tongue, with the
nausea (first day), 1 '.—Dorsum of tongue sore on right side, causing painful
mastication and deglutition (fifteenth day); rightside of tongue inflamed
not swollen (sixteenth day), 6 '.—Feeling as if the tongue had been cut in the
middle, and was just healing up, at 10 a.m. (fifth day), 6 .—Tongue feeling
as if it had been scalded ; the whole upper surface feels as after taking
Aconite (after three hours), 4 '.—Tongue felt as if it were scalded, all day
(first day), 4 '.—Tongue feeling as if it had been burned (after two hours,
second day), 4 '.—Acrid feeling in the tongue (after six hours, second day), 4 '.
— [280.] Biting sensation in the tongue, with increased secretion of saliva
(third day), 4 '.—Stinging, biting sensation all over the tongue (after three
hours, third day), 4 '.—Tougue smarts and prickles, and burns a little (elev¬
enth to fourteenth day), 12 .—Slight pains about the root of the tougue, worse
on left side (after five hours), 13 .— General Mouth. Soft palate and
uvula inflamed (fifteenth day), 6 '.—Breath hot (twenty-first day), 6 '.—Mouth
and throat dry (fifth day), 5 .—Mouth and throat very dry (sixth night), 5 .—
Parched mouth, on awaking (second day), 2 .—Bitterness in the mouth, with
dryness (after forty-five minutes), 1 '.— [290.] Dryness of the mouth, with
bitter taste (after one hour and fifty-five minutes), 1 '.—Great dryness of the
mouth, at 11.15 p.m. (second day), 1 '.—Dryness of the mouth (fifth day), 1 '.—
Saliva. Saliva very profuse; ran from the mouth during sleep, and wet
the pillow (first night); saliva flowed from mouth very profusely during the
night (second night) ; perceptible increase in the flow of saliva (third
day); troublesome drivelling (third night); saliva not so troublesome (fourth
night) ; unusual quantity of saliva, thin and w T atery (fifth day) ; drivelling
(fifth night); great increase in the amount of the saliva (sixth day), 2 .—
During the afternoon noticed an increase in the amount of saliva. Spit¬
ting became frequent, though unusual in health (third day) ; saliva is
greatly increased in quantity, and keeps up a constant drivelling while

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

185

lying on the face (fourth day); saliva very abundant at 12.30; not trou¬
blesome at 9 p.m. (fifth day) ; an unusual amount of saliva has troubled the
prover ever since, 5 *.—Increased flow of saliva that tastes saltish (after three
hours, third day), 4c .—Increased secretion of saliva, with biting sensation in
the tongue (third day), 4 '.—Slight ptyalism (seventh, eighth, ninth, eleventh
to fourteenth day), 12 .—Slight salivation (twenty-seventh day), 12 .— Taste .
In the morning everything tastes and smells sour (twenty-third day), 6 *.—
[300.] Bitter taste in the mouth, with the colic (fifth morning), 6 *.—Peculiar
bitter, herbv taste, 13 .—Bitter taste in the mouth (sixth and twelfth days), 1 ;
(second and fifth days), 1 '; (thirty-first day), 6 *.—Bitter taste in mouth, with
absence of thirst (fifth day), lb .—Bitter taste in the mouth, with dryness
(sixth night), 1 *.—Brassy taste in the mouth (sixth day), 10 *.—Rough, flat
taste in the mouth (third day), 4 '.—The taste of the medicine continually
returning in gusts to the mouth; a feeling as if vomiting would relieve
(after half an hour), 1 '.—At dinner all food seemed tasteless (second day), 1 *.
—Food has not its natural taste (seventh day), 1 *.— [310.] Food has an un¬
natural taste, as on recovery from a long illness (fifth day), lb .—Nothing
tastes natural (after two hours, second day), 4 '.— Speech . Unable to speak
aloud for some time, on waking (seventh morning), 5 .

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Throat ulcerated on right side (sixteenth day); throat bitter
(seventeenth day), 6 *.—Throat sore on right side, at 8 p.m. (thirteenth day);
at 2 p.m. ; passed off about 4 p.m. (fourteenth day), 6 *.—Throat sore, grow¬
ing worse in the afternoon (fourth day) ; worse (fifth day), 6 .—Throat sore
(twenty-first day), 6 *.—Slight burning in throat (eighth day), 12 .—Before ris¬
ing felt pricking pains through and in the throat, particularly in the tonsils
aud larvux, lasting several minutes, and quite severe (third morning), 11 .—
Unpleasant feeling in the throat, all the afternoon (sixth day), 5 .— [ 320 .]
Sense of dryness, high up in the throat, apparently back of the palate
(after five hours), 13 . — Fauces. Soreness and inflammation of fauces,
worse on right side (fifteenth day), 6 *.—Roughness of the fauces, with feel¬
ing as if vomiting would come on (in a few minutes, first day), 1 .—Fauces
feel sore (fourth day), 4 *.— Pharynx. Hawking of mucus from the pha¬
rynx (after three hours), 1 '.—Choking feeling in the pharynx, with slight
vertigo (after thirteen hours, third day), 1 *.—Constriction of the pharynx,
at 1.30 and 9 p.m. (third day), 2 .— (Esophagus. Heat and dryness of
the oesophagus, as before (sixth day), 5 .—A distressing feeling of emptiness in
oesophagus (thirty-first day), 6 *.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Appetite. At supper voracious appetite, followed by
pain in the epigastric region (sixth day), 1 *.—[330.] * Appetite voracious
(seventh day), 1 *.—Increasing appetite (third and fourth days) ; hungry
all the time (fifth day) ; awoke with hunger and headace, both of which
passed off after a hearty breakfast (eighth day), 5 *.—Appetite somewhat in¬
creased, at 9 p.m. (third day), 5 .—Was quite hungry, but did not eat very
heartily (second evening); had an abnormal appetite, but his food did not
distress him (third morning) ; appetite remained quite good for two weeks
(after the proving), 8 .—Appetite about the same as usual, except he gets tired
before he gets through eating (fifth day) ; less appetite (tenth day), 10 *.—The
appetite was much increased for the first few days of the proving, after
which it diminished ; no particular loathing of food, but rather an indiffer¬
ence to it, 11 .—Appetite was indifferently good, but food still tasteless (after fif¬
teen and a half hours, second day), 1 *.—At dinner the appetite not as good as
usual, though before the proving it had been keen. Throughout the meal
the same faint nausea persisted (first day), 1 *.—Appetite good at dinner, but

186

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

entirely absent at supper-time (first day), 1 .—Little appetite for breakfast;
the bread seemed tasteless (second day), 1 *.— [340.] At dinner appetite very
poor, after driving in the cool air all the forenoon (first day), lb .—Appetite
deficient (fifth day), lb .—Very little appetite, after eleven hours’ abstinence,
with a strong repugnauce to butter (after four hours and thirty-five min¬
utes), 10 .—Appetite at breakfast poor, with the usual repugnance to butter
(second day), lc .—Deficient appetite, with pain in liver (fourth day), lc .—
Appetite at breakfast very poor, with muddled feeling in the head (seventh
day), lc .—Appetite poor; ate a light breakfast, which seemed to afford some
relief (seventh day), 2 .—Appetite not very good (third day), 2 *.—Appetite
poor (third, fourth, and fifth days), 3 .—Appetite all gone (fourth day), 2 *.—
[350.] No appetite (ninth day), 6 .—Unusual hunger, craving for acid food, at
6 a.m. (fifth day), 2 .—Desire for acid food (fourth and fifth days), 3 .—Before
taking the dose had a good appetite, but after swallowing it, found that he
could not bear the sight or smell of food, especially of roast beef, lc .—At din¬
ner, marked repugnance to butter and fatty foods (second day), lb .—At break¬
fast, repugnance to butter ; even a small quantity aggravates the epigastric
pain (sixth day), lb .—At dinner, a complete repugnauce to animal food,
although there was less nausea than on the preceding day; unable to eat rich
pudding, of which he is ordinarily fond (third day), 1 *.—At dinner, complete
disgust at animal food, unable to eat any, and the appetite was very poor
(fourth day), 1 *.— Thirst • Thirsty and drank a great deal of water (fourth
and fifth days), 3 .—Thirsty, with a dry feeling all over the system (ninth
day), 2 .—[360.] Thirsty (half an hour after fourth dose), 2 .—Absence of
thirst, with bitter taste in mouth (fifth day),' b .—No thirst (second day), 1 *.
— Eructations and Hiccough. — Frequent eructations of wind
from the stomach (thirty-first day), 6a .—Eructations of sour fluid from the
stomach (first day), 4 .—Eructations, with a bitter taste in the mouth, caus¬
ing nausea and abortive attempts at vomiting (after four hours and twenty
minutes, second day), lb .—Eructations of a bitter taste, with slight nausea
(after seven hours and a half), lb .—Eructations, almost bringing on emesis
(fourth day),’ 0 . — Eructations tasting of rotten eggs (fourth day), la .—
Eructations tasting of the medicine, with increased nausea (after forty-
five minutes), 10 .— [370.] Regurgitation tasting of the medicine, but with
little nausea (after half an hour, third day), 11 .—Eructations tasting of
Ptelea (after three hours and twenty minutes), 10 .—Rising of bitter fluid,
with a deathly nausea, confusion of the head, and sweat on forehead, at 1
a.m. (fifth day), 1 .—Sour risings from the stomach, at'4 p.m. (fifth day), 1 . —
Sour risings from the stomach, with feeling of weight and uneasiness in the
stomach (after six hours and fifty minutes, third day), 1 *.—Eructation of
wind (after first and second doses, third day), 2 *.—Hiccough, at 3 p.m.
(third day), 5 .— Heartburn. Awoke in afterpart of the night with heart¬
burn, and a sensation of fine, violent, agitation of all the muscles of the
body and limbs, worse in hands and fingers ; this sensation passed away grad¬
ually in about five minutes (first night), 7 .— Nausea and Vomiting.
Some nausea, 13 .—Severe nausea for five minutes, with distress in the umbilicus,
and dull, pressive headache (after eight hours), 4 *.— [380.] Constant nausea
(one hour after second dose), 7 *.—Slight but persistent nausea, not at all disa¬
greeable, somewhat resembling the effect of a few inhalations of sulphuric
ether, at 9.30 a.m. (first day), 1 .—Slight but persistent nausea, from 9 till 11
p.m. (first day), 1 .—Nausea, with pressive feeling at the base of the brain
(first day), 1 .—Nausea, with feverish heat and pain in the limbs (second
day), 1 .—Increased nausea, with heat of skin and profuse perspiration on

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

187

the forehead, after dinner (third and fourth days), 1 .—Nausea all the after¬
noon and evening, with splitting headache, incapacitating for mental
exertion (fifth day), 1 .—Persistent nausea and vomiting, with giddiness of
the head, and a feeling as if unsteady in the legs (tenth day), 1 .—Some
nausea for two minutes, with efforts to vomit (after six hours, third day), 4 ®.—
Sensation of nausea (soon after first dose), 2 .— [ 390 .] Nausea fora few min¬
utes (after fourth dose), 2 .—Nausea, with full, throbbing headache and diz¬
ziness (ten minutes after second dose, second day), 2 .—Slight nausea, at 5
P.M. (fourth day), 2 .—A very mild nausea, by no means unpleasant, lasted
during the whole forenoon (first day), 1 *.—Slight nausea, rising from the
stomach upwards, accompanied by roughness of the back part of the tongue
(first dav), u .—Nausea and pressing pain in the forehead ; the pain presses
from within outwards (first day), la . — At 9.30 p.m., nausea, with rumbling in
the bowels, accompanied with discharge of flatus, with desire for stool (first
day), 1 *.—Nausea, aggravated by lying down (first day),' a .—Singing increases
the nausea, and aggravates the headache, causing shooting pains from within
outwards (second day), la .—Nausea is much worse on walking (after eight
hours and a half, second day), la .— [ 400 .] Less nausea; stomach feels
weak (third day),' 3 .—Pressure aggravates the nausea (sixth day), 1 ®.—Speak¬
ing aggravated the nausea (after forty-five minutes), 1 ®.—Rising aggravates
the nausea (after one hour and forty-five minutes), 1 ®.—Slight nausea (after
first dose) ; nausea (soon after first and second doses, second day), 2 ®.—Feel¬
ing of nausea (after third dose, second day), 3 .—Mild nausea, with slight
griping pain in stomach, preceded and accompanied the vertigo (after eight
hours, second day), lb .—Nausea (thirty-first day), 6 *.—Slight feeling of nausea,
with the hard pain in the epigastrium (sixth day), 5 *.—Slight nausea (after
second dose), 11 . —[410.] Burning and qualmishness at the stomach, with
pain on pressure (after forty-five minutes), 1 ®.—Qualmishness increased (after
forty-five minutes), 1 ®.—Qualmishness of the stomach, with weight and pain
in the right hypochondriac region (after eight hours, fourth day), lb .—
Retching, with increase of frontal headache (third and fourth days), 1 .—
Nausea and vomiting soon followed, although no relief came after the
vomiting (twelfth day), 1 .— Stomach. Rumbling in the stomach, with
inclination to vomit (soon), 1 ®.—Stomach sour (sixth day), 10 ’.—Sour stom¬
ach and a dull, heavy pain, extending around the small of the back, after
taking the drug (fifth day), 10 *.—Slight sickness at stomach (tenth day), 12 .
—Epigastric region is sore to touch (sixth day), 1 *.— [ 420 .] When awake,
during night, felt that the weight at the stomach was much worse than
during the day (third night), 1 *.—At breakfast he ate some pudding; symp¬
toms all aggravated at once, especially the heaviness at the stomach and the
difficulty of concentrating thought (fourth day), 1 *.—At dinner ate roast beef
and pudding; pain and distress in the stomach soon after, with feeling as if
a stone were there (fifth day), la .—Awoke with a weight at the stomach (sixth
day), la .—An immediate feeling of heaviness in the stomach (after first
and second doses, third day), 2 ®.—Burden in stomach, soon after dinner (sec¬
ond day), 2 .—Weight and fulness in the stomach, one hour after eating a
light breakfast (after one hour and a quarter), 1 ').—A very moderate meal
was followed in half an hour by a sensation of stuffing and fulness (second
day), lb .—Weight in the stomach, with bloatingin the abdomen, on waking
(second day), Ib .—Awakened at 1 A.M. by a pressing pain in the stomach ;
a feeling as of a weight; worse on motion, and aggravated by pressure
with the hands (fifth day), 1 .— [ 430 .] Constant distress in the epigastric re¬
gion and right hypochoudrium, with drawing pains in the fingers and

188

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

ankles, for one hour (after six hours, fifth day) ; not so severe (sixth day ), 4b .
—Dull distress in the stomach, with fine stitches in the right temple (after
forty minutes), 40 .—Constant distress in the stomach, with darting pains in
right temple (after one hour), 40 .—Breakfast relieved the distress in the
stomach (after one hour and ten minutes), 40 .—Frequent distress in the
stomach (first day), 40 .—Distress in the epigastrium (after two hours, second
day), 40 .—Burning distress in the epigastrium (not severe), (third day), 40 .—
Distress in the epigastric region (after one hour), 4a .—Oppression at the epi¬
gastrium, at 11 a.m. (third day), 2 . — Attended to his duties as usual, but
felt such an oppression and weakness at the stomach that he had no heart
to work (third day),' a .— [440.] Faint feeling in the stomach, with sourish
rising (after eight hours and a half, second day), 14 .—A faint feeling in
stomach (fifth day), 5 .—Stomach feels empty (fourth day), 6 .—Empty feeling
in stomach, after dinner (first day), 2 .—Immediately after eating dinner
the stomach seemed perfectly empty ; very troublesome sensation of gone¬
ness (eighth day), 2 .—Slight burning in stomach (eighth day), 12 .— *Pressure
as of a stone at the pit of the stomach, aggravated by a light meal (third day), 10 .
—^Pressure in the stomach, after a light meal (fifth day), lb .—Soreness at
pit of stomach (third day), 3 .—Pain at the stomach follows every meal
(seventh day), 1 ®.— [450.] Pain in stomach and umbilicus set in with vigor
(after third dose, third day), 2 ®.—Pain in the epigastric region after supper
(sixth day), 14 .—Pain in stomach (fourth day), 2 .—Griping in the stomach,
with sharp pain on slight pressure (after three hours and fifty minutes), 16 .—
Griping, contractive pain in the stomach, for half an hour (after four
hours), 10 .—Griping in the epigastric region (fifth day), 10 .—Griping pain in
the epigastrium, aggravated by speaking and by deep respiration; pressure
aggravates the pain and causes nausea (after forty minutes, third day), lb .—
In bed the griping pain in the epigastric region worse than during the day,
and the abdomen swollen, but not painful (second day), 1 ®.—Occasional
sharp pains in the stomach (fifth day), 4 \—Rapid motion causes sharp pain
in the right epigastric and hypochondriac regions (second day), 10 .— [460.]
At 9 A.M., felt a hard pain in the epigastrium, with slight feeling of nausea
for about five minutes, and afterwards, three or four times during the day
(sixth day), 5 ®.—When bending the body, cramplike pains in cardiac region
(twelfth day), 6 *.—Slight colicky pain in the epigastric region (fourth day), 4 .
—In the afternoon frequent, cutting pains in the epigastric and umbilical
regions (first day), 46 .—Severe aching pain in the stomach, with giddiness
(seventh day), 1 .—Aching pains, with occasional sticking in the region of the
diaphragm (third day), 1 ®.—Continued speaking, even for five minutes,
causes stitching pains in the diaphragm (second day), lb .—A squeezing pain
in the epigastric region (after thirteen and three-quarter hours, second
day), 1 ®.—Throbbing paiu in the epigastric region, aggravated by full and
deep respiration (fifth day), 1 ®.—Awakened by gastric and hepatic symp¬
toms, all of which are aggravated towards morning (sixth day), 10 .—[470.]
Eating a very small piece of cheese aggravated all the gastric and hepatic
symptoms (second day), 10 . — Feeling as of sand in the stomach, at 5 p.m.
(fourth day), 2 .—Some unpleasant sensation in stomach, at 9 p.m. (first
day), 5 .—Evident signs of gastralgia (fourth day), 2 .

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Hypochondria. Constant feeling of weight in the
hypochondria, when walking ; a dragging pain which affects the right as
well as the left side (eleventh day), 1 .—Pain and soreness, extending from
the right to the left hypochondriac regions, but worse in the epigastric
region ; a feeling of weight, aggravated by standing erect or sitting erect,

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

189

and relieved by stooping forward (six hours and a half after first dose,
sixth dav), la .—Frequent drawing pains in the right and left hypochon-
drium (fifth day), 4 ®.—Slight swelling in the region of the liver (sixth day), 1 ®.
—The liver is perceptibly swollen, and sore on pressure, which causes a
dull and aching pain (seventh day), 1 *.—Griping in the bowels, with swell¬
ing of the liver, which is tender to pressure (after eight hours), 1 '.—[ 480 .]
The right hypochondriac region is swollen, and the clothes feel too tight
(fifth day), lb .—Lying on the left side, the liver dragging on the ligaments,
and swollen and tender even to a light touch (first night), 1 '.—Eating a
very small piece of cheese aggravated all the hepatic and gastric symp¬
toms (second day), 1 '.—Heavy aching pain in the liver, with deficient appe¬
tite (fourth day), 1 '.—Weight and pain in the liver, relieved by lying on
the right side ; aggravated by lying on the left, which causes a dragging
pain (fifth day), 1 '.—Awakened by hepatic and gastric symptoms, all of
which are aggravated, towards morning (sixth day), 1 '.—Dull heavy pain in
the right hypochondriac region, apparently on the convex surface of the
liver (fifth day), 13 .—Feeling of weight, and dull pain in the right hypo¬
chondriac region, with qualmishness of the stomach (after eight hours,
fourth day), lb .—Stitching pains in the right hypochondriac region, which
is swolleu, with aggravated lumbar pains (after eight hours, fifth day), lb .—■
Increase of the hepatic pains after a light meal (fifth day), 11 ’.—[ 490 .]
Hepatic pain aggravated (sixth day), lb .—Liver feels heavy and sore, espe¬
cially when lying on the left side (seventh day), lb .—Dull pain in region of
liver, at 2 p.m. (sixth day), 5 .—Rapid motion causes sharp pains in the
right hypochondriac and epigastric region (second day), 1 '.—During the
whole forenoon, sharp pains in the right hypochondriac region (fifth day), 1 .
—Occasional pains in right hypochondrium, shooting downwards (eleventh
day), 6 ®.—On rising, pain in the right hypochondrium, disappearing on
pressure (fourth morning), 6 .—At 10 p.m., a sharp cutting pain in the right
hypochondriac region, aggravated by deep inspiration, sufficiently severe
to prevent sleep (fourth day), 11 .—Steady cutting pain in right hypochon¬
drium, at 4 p.m. (fourteenth day), 6 . — Pains shoot from right hypochondrium
downwards (fourth day), 6 .—[ 500 .] Shooting and throbbing pains in right
hypogastrium (twenty-sixth day), 6 *.—Throbbing pains in the right liypo-
choudrium, at 8 p.m. (eighth day), 6 .—Occasional stitches in right hypo¬
chondrium (third day), 61 .—Constant distress in the right hypochondrium
and epigastric region, with drawing pains in the fingers and ankles, for one
hour (after six hours, fifth day); same, but not so severe (sixth day), 4b .—
All the evening had a drawing aching distress in the right hypochondrium
(first day)/ 1 .—Drawing distress in right hypochondrium (fourth day), 4 .—
Severe distress in the region of the spleen (after half an hour), 41 .—Severe
distress in the region of the spleen and right side of umbilicus, with pres-
sive feeling in forehead, during the forenoon (second day), 41 .—Frequent
fine pains in the region of the spleen, and in the fingers (after eight hours), 41 .
—Acute cutting pain in the spleen, at 11.35 a.m. (third day), 1 '.—[ 510 .]
Tenderness of the splenic region, with soreness to the touch (eighth day), 1 .
—The pain in splenic region much increased, and the swelling evidently
greater (eleventh day), 1 .—Splenic pain much aggravated (twelfth day), 1 .—
Umbilical Hey ion. Umbilical region very tender, and seemingly on
the point of aching (third day), 21 .—Rumbling in the umbilical region, with
swelling, accompanied by slight vertigo, with sweat on the forehead (after
six hours), lb .—Pulsations in umbilicus isochronous with those of the heart
(after second dose), 7 *.—In the evening, the feeling of uneasiness in the

190

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

bowels (umbilical region) came on, increasing in severity until 9, when it
was almost intolerable. It was of a peculiar character, bearing down,
sometimes spasmodic, and griping ; sometimes sharp and throbbing. This
really severe attack passed off by midnight, and sleep brought entire relief
(sixth day), 2 .—Feeling of uneasiness in umbilical region (one hour after
second dose), 7 *.—Dull pains in the umbilical region, quite severe, continu¬
ing half an hour, at 8 p.m. (second day), 2 .—Dull heavy pain in umbilical
region (after second dose), 7 *.— [ 520 .] Dull heavy aching in region of um¬
bilicus (half an hour after fourth dose), 7 *.—Dull, heavy, passive pain around
the umbilicus, with a fine, active pain above the umbilicus, across the ab¬
domen; relieved by pressure (half an hour after second dose, third day), 7 .
—Dull, constant, heavy pain in the umbilical region (after one hour, fourth
day), 7 . — Several times through the afternoon and evening had sharp
colicky pains in the umbilical region (second day), 4c .—Slight colicky pains
in the umbilical region (third day), 4c .—After going to bed, colicky pains
in umbilical region, with a desire to press it, but pressure aggravates;
better on rising (fourth day); similar but not quite so severe, after going
to bed (fifth day), 6 .—Colic pains below umbilicus (ninth day),A—5 p.m.,
colicky pains in the umbilicus for the last hour (fourth day), 4b .—Sharp
pains in the umbilicus (after one hour, fourth day), 4h .—In the abdomen,
frequent cutting pains in the umbilical and epigastric region (first day), 4b .
—[ 530 .] Distress in the umbilicus, with dull pressive headache, aud nau¬
sea (after eight hours), 4 *.—Almost constant cutting pains in the left um¬
bilical aud epigastric region, with aching distress in the right hypochon-
drium (third day), 4 *.—About 5 p.m., the old pain in the umbilical region
became a prominent symptom, and continued without intermission, rather
severe (second day); pain in umbilicus and stomach set in with vigor (after
third dose, third day) ; pain and tenderness in umbilicus continued all day
(fifth day), 2 *.—The abdominal pain extends more towards the umbilical
region, and is worse on motion. On drawing a long breath, a sharp stitch
proceeds from the umbilicus towards the backbone, and the tenderness on
pressure is increased (ninth day), 1 . — General Abdomen. Bowels
slightly distended at night, aud feeling like diarrhoea (sixth day),A—
Bloating of the abdomen, with weight in the stomach, on waking (second
day),A—Abdomen bloated (first night), ,c .—The abdomen much swollen,
and tender over its whole extent, especially over the splenic region (tenth
day), 1 .—In bed, the abdomen swollen but not painful (second day), 1 *.—
A geueral change iu the system seemed to have taken place, and the former
weary feeling supervened, with tenderness of the abdominal viscera, i. e.,
readiness to become painful (after third dose), 2 *.— [ 540 .] Abdominal ten¬
derness increased after the vertigo (eighth day), 1 .—Bumbling in the bowels
followed by diarrhmic stool (after dose, fourth day), 2 *.—Frequent rumbling
in the bowels, with desire for stool (third day), 4 *.—Rumbling in bowels, at
2 p.m. (first day), 5 .—Rumbling in bowels (eighth day), 5 *.—Rumbling iu
the bowels, at 1.30 p.m. (third day), 2 .—Rumbling iu the bowels, with ten¬
derness on pressure (sixth day), lh .—Rumbling iu the bowels after stool
(after four hours and twenty minutes), lc .—Griping aud rumbling in abdo¬
men continued (second day), lc .—Pain and rumbling in the bowels, as if

—Flatulence (third day), 2 .—Involuntary discharge of flatus, with urging
to stool (fifteen minutes after second dose), lb .—Borborygmus (fourth day), 2 .
—Some colic after retiring at night (third day) ; colic pains iu the morn-

191

ing before rising, with discharge of flatulence ; after going to bed at night,
colic, with emission of flatulence and borborygmus; awakens from sleep
(fourth day); before rising, colic with excessively bitter taste in the mouth;
colic disappears on motiou, but comes on at intervals all day, with frequent
discharge of wind from the bowels (fifth day); about noon, severe colic,

men and stomach (half an hour after second dose, third day), 71 .—Soreness

vated more by bending the body in any direction than by pressure ; the
soreness or heaviness of the bowels is such as to incline him, when sitting
or walking, to support the abdomen with the hands, indicating a moderate
degree of congestion of the abdominal viscera (fifth day) ; bowels not so
sore (sixth day), 10 \—Griping in the bowels, with rumbling, and pressure
in the rectum ; pressure increased the griping (first night), 10 .— [ 560 .] Dull
pain in abdomen (half an hour after second dose, third day), 71 .—After a
restless dream, haunted slumber till 1 a.m. ; awoke with a seated, dull,
heavy pain in the abdominal regiou, felt distinctly in the liver, which was
easiest when lying on the right side (first night), 10 .—Constant distress in
the small intestines, with an urgency to stool (after three hours), 41 .—Fre¬
quent distress in the bowels, during forenoon (first day), 41 .—Constant ach¬
ing distress in the whole abdomen (second day), 41 .—Aching distress in
bowels, back, and legs, all the forenoon (fourth day), 41 .—Slight distress in
the abdomen, in the forenoon (third day), 4b .—Pain in abdomen very severe
(after third dose, third day) ; whole abdomidal region began to ache and
pain, on a sudden movement (one hour and a half after dose, fourth day) ;
abdominal pain settled to a steady dull pain, not so severe as before (after
five hours, fourth day) ; bowel pains continued (fifth day). It was full
three weeks before pressure on the abdomen could be endured without
pain/ 1 .—Awoke with the same pain in the bowels as the night before, at
5.30 a.m.; at 10 a.m., pain in bowels came on with redoubled vigor; 1
p.m., pain less (seventh day), 2 .—Had repeated colicky pains in the small
intestines, lasting but a minute or two at a time, in the evening (first day), 4b .
— [ 570 .] Colicky pains in the small intestines, every few minutes for one
hour (after fourteen hours, third day), 4 .—Colic pains came on earlier than
yesterday, but are of short duration (sixth day), 6 .—At 9 p.m. (in bed),
sharp thin pain across abdomen, from side to side, half an inch above um¬
bilicus; comes in flashes, at intervals of about one minute; relieved by
pressure (first day), 7 .—Pain in the bowels, in the morning (eighth day), 5 .—
Awoke three or four times during the night, with hard pain in the bowels
(sixth night), 5 . — Pain moved downwards to the abdomen (after four
hours), 10 .—Occasional pains in the bowels (first day), 40 .—Occasional flying
pains in the abdomen (after three hours),V—Occasional pains in various
parts of the abdomen throughout the day (fourth day), 6 .—Aching in the
bowels, while walking; on standing still ; pain aggravated by deep inspi¬
ration (fourth day),' 1 .— [ 580 .] When lying on the back, a feeling of pres¬
sure on abdomen (sixth day), 61 .—Beating in abdomen (four hours and a
half after fourth dose), 7 *.—Uneasiness in the bowels, with flatulence, at 10
p.m. (fifth day), 2 .—Bowels soon felt tendency to diarrhoea (seventh day), 51 .
—Abdomen weak, lax (after second dose), 71 . — Abdomen feels hollow,
empty, caved in (after one hour, fourth day), 7 .—Abdomen felt caved in
(one hour after second dose); with sense of heat (after fourth dose), 71 .—
Sensation of softness in abdomen, and as if its front walls were drawn in

192

towards the spine (after second dose), 7 \— Hypogastrium and Iliac
Region. Distress in hypogastric region, with mushy stool (after four
hours, first day), 4 .—Pain in the hypogastrium in the region of the bladder,
continued fifteen minutes (one hour after second dose, second day)/.—
[ 590 .] Griping pains, with rumbling in the right iliac fossa (after four
hours and a quarter, sixth day), 14 .—Steady pain in left hypogastrium, con¬
tinuing several hours (twenty-seventh day), 6 *.—Colicky pains in the hypo-
gastrium before stool, in the evening (second day), 4b .—Some colic pains in

Rectum and Anus. —Old pressure at rectum returned (after forty-
five minutes), 1 '. — Pressure in rectum aggravated by rising (after one

(first night), lc .—Pressure on the rectum, such as precedes a dysenteric pas¬
sage (second day). 1 '.—Pressure in rectum is worse as night advances (sec¬
ond day), 1 '. — [ 600 .] Violent urging to stool (after two hours and twenty
minutes); renewed urging (after two hours and thirty-five minutes) ; urg¬
ing to stool, and a sudden discharge of a quantity of thin diarrhoeic faeces
(after four hours and twenty minutes), 1 '.—Straining at stool, with increase
of vertigo (after seven hours and forty-minutes), lb .—Urging to stool, but it

(after eleven hours and a half, second day), lb .—Urging to stool; a con¬
tinued pressure ou the rectum, but on attempting to have passage it re¬

day) ; urging in rectum aggravated (sixth day); pressure less (seventh

— At 5 p.m., urging to stool, at an unusual time (first day), 1 .—Urging to
stool, with rumbling in the bowels, from 6 a.m. till 3 p.m. (seventh day), 1 .
—In the evening had severe urging to stool; it was very loose and dark-
colored (first day); awakened at 9 p.m., by painful urging to stool; it
proved to be another attack of diarrhoea ; quantity small, but with much
pain throughout the bowels (fourth day), 101 .—Feels as though diarrhoea
was coming ; desire for stool, tenesmus, but no stool, at 7 p.m. (sixth day), 5 .
—A sensation as if diarrhoea would come on (soon after sixth dose, third
day), 11 .— [ 610 .] Stool followed by tenesmus, and succeeded by itching and
smarting of the anus (fourth dav), lc .—Distress in the anus following natural
stool (after two hours), 1 .—Smarting like piles after a hard stool (eighth
day), 5 .—Smarting of the anus, with discharge of diarrhoeic faeces (after
four hours and twenty minutes), 1 '.

Stool, — Diarrhoea. Diarrhoeic stool (fourth day); diarrhoea; five
stools during the day (fifth day) ; some diarrhoea (sixth day) ; diarrhoea
(seventh day), 3 .—Diarrhoeic stool, very dark in color and sulphuric, in
smell, followed rumbling in the bowels (fourth day); three stools during
the day, rather diarrhoeic (fifth day) ; diarrhoeic stool continued a full
week, when the unnatural condition was removed, 21 .—The prover was
naturally of a costive habit, and was costive when he commenced the prov¬
ing; but, after taking the drug, the bowels moved regularly every morn¬
ing, without any particular uneasiness, for two or three days, when symp¬
toms of diarrhoea came on, which, however, amounted only to one thorough

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

193

operation as from cathartic action ; after this the bowels became consti¬
pated again, there being no movement for two or three days at a time, 11 .—
Stool at first of natural consistence, but towards the close thinner and diar-

diarrhoeic faeces, with smarting of the anus (after four hours and twenty

what thinner in consistence, and even more cadaverous in smell (after
seven hours); a discharge of faeces coated with slime; the passage is fol¬
lowed by tenesmus, which brings on a small discharge of faeces, with a

charge thinner than usual (first day), 1 .—Stool of a mushy character, with dis¬
tress in the hypogastric region (after four hours, first days), 4 .—Mushy stool

day), 4 .—Lumpy, dark-colored stool (second day), 40 .—Natural but lumpy
stool (after three hours), 40 .—Stools, yesterday and to-day, of usual consist¬
ence and slimy coating (third day), 1 *.— Constipation. [ 630 .] * Consti¬
pation (sixth day), 11 .—Constipation ; no morning stool as usual, but at 7
p.m., small hard stool, after much straining (third and fourth day), 1 .—
Bowels costive (sixth day), 10a .—Stool rather constipated (second day), 4 *.—
For three days has had no stool till to-day; stool nearly natural (fifth
day); no stool for two days (seventh day) ; hard stool, at 9 a.m. (eighth
day); less tendency to costiveness (three or four days after leaving off
drug), 5 .—No passage from bowels to-day, a very unusual occurrence (first

rectum (fifth day), lb .—No stool (sixth day), lc .— [ 640 .] Hard and difficult
stool, with smarting of the anus, after the passage (eighth day), 1 .—Hard
and difficult stool, at 9 a.m. (tenth day), 1 .—At 4 p.m., hard stool, with
straining (fourth day), 1 .

Urinated 5 ounces (2 ounces more than normal quantity) at 6 p.m., 5|

sections.text:
[ 670 .] In the evening, walls of chest feel as if they had not
power to expand when breathing (twelfth day), 6 *.—The effects mentioned
in the proving have gradually declined. The only new phase consists in
a number of thoracic symptoms, which have come on very gradually, and
which now cause considerable pain. As the various gastric and hepatic
symptoms declined, uneasiness and difficulty in breathing came on, with dull
pain, especially in the right infraclavicular region, accompanied by hack¬
ing cough without expectoration. This has come on very insidiously, and
now the right lung is dull on percussion, especially in the right infraclav¬
icular region. On auscultating the region over the bifurcation of the
trachea and the upper part of the sternum (with Cammann’s stethoscope),
the respiration was found to be tubular, the sound was higher in pitch than
the normal vesicular sound, and more rapidly evolved. Expiration and
inspiration were of equal length, with a slight interval between them. On
making a full inspiration, sharp pains shot from the sternum towards the

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

195

nipples, especially that of the left side. Pressure on the intercostal spaces
close to the sternum caused pain of a dull aching nature. These thoracic
symptoms were better in the house, and aggravated by exposure to the
keen air (eleventh day); thoracic symptoms had gradually declined
(eighteenth day), 11 .—Pain in the lower part of each lung, in the evening
(sixth day), 101 .—A sharp darting pain through upper lobe of left lung,
lasting only a short time, but returning every half hour; aggravated by

terior mediastinum were aggravated during the attack of vertigo (second

Pulse 88 (first day) ; 96, small and hard (third and fourth days); 96,

but not rapid (third evening); pulse more rapid, 90 (fourth morning);
more natural than on preceding day, at 12.30 p.m. (fourth day) ; pulse

—Pulse 80 (first day); 74 (second day)/*.—Pulse 88, soft and weak (after

and seventh days); 84 (eighth day)/ 1 .—Pulse 104, quick, small, and

day); 80, in the morning; 92, at 11 a.m. (after ironing an hour); 88,
and occasionally intermitting, at 5 p.m. (sixth day); 75, in morning; 106,

Neck and liack .— [ 700 .] Neck. Pain in back of neck, at 6 p.m.
(fourth day), 5 .—Cords of neck lame on the right side (fifth morning), 5 .—
Whole neck feels swollen, about noon (fifth day), 5 .—Pain in back of neck,

196

about noon (fifth day), 5 .—In the afternoon, the nape of the neck grows stiff,
causing painful tension when moving (twenty-second day), 6 \ — jSflcJi.
Lameness in the back on getting up (third day), 5 .—Back somewhat lame
on waking (sixth day), 5 .—Awoke with backache (seventh morning), 5 .—
Backache (eighth day), 5 .—Hard backache the whole length of spine and
back of neck, also through right shoulder, at 7 p.m. (seventh day), 5 .—
[710.] Dull backache (third day), 4 *.—Awoke with severe backache, which

(sixth day), 45 .— Dorstll. Dull aching pain in the left scapula, aggravated

all the regions, but especially the dorsal (fifth night), 15 .—Aching-drawing
pain in the left scapula and shoulder-joint, at 2.40 p-m. (third day), lc .—
[720.] Rending tearing pain in the left scapula (first night), lc .— Lum¬
bar. Dull aching pain in the small of the back (seventh day), 11 .—Dull
heavy pain, extending around the small of the back (fifth day) ; the sore¬
ness or lameness of the lumbar region is worse (sixth day); pain in the
lumbar region most of the time (seventh and tenth days), 10 *.—On awaking,
had a pain in the small of the back, which ceased after rising, leaving, for
a while, a tired feeling (sixth morning), 51 .—Aching distress in the small of
the back, knees, and calves of the legs (fifth day), 4 *.—Dull aching distress
in the small of the back (second day), 4 *.—Dull aching pain in the small
of the back, aggravated by motion, at 11 a.m. (third day), lc .—Became
conscious of a dull aching pain in the small of the back; motion adds a
sharp sticking pain to the dull one (fourth day), 10 .—On getting up, had a
feeling of lameness' in small of back (second day), 0 .—Severe backache,
worse in lumbar region, at 2 p.m. (sixth day), 5 . — [ 730 .] Severe aching dis¬
tress in the whole lumbar and sacral region, in the afternoon (third day), 4 b.
—Awoke with severe pain in the lumbar region (fourth day), 4 *.—Awak¬
ened, at 4 a.m., by the severity of the lumbar pain (fifth day), le .—Lumbar
pains aggravated, with stitching pains in the right hypochondriac region,
which is swollen (after eight hours, fifth day), 15 .—Feels lame in the region
of the kidneys, on waking (seventh morning), 5 *.—(Thinks the provings
have improved the condition of the kidneys), 5 ®.—Very severe pain in right
kidney (tenth day), 11 .—When walking, a cramplike pain in the sacral
region, left side, so severe that he has to stand still until it passes off (tenth
day), 6 *.

Aching of all the limbs, especially of the flexor mus¬
cles (sixth day), 1 *.—Aching in the limbs, in the afternoon (sixth day), 11 .—
[ 740 .] Awoke at 6, with a bruised sensation in all the limbs, especially
worse in the muscles of the back. The sore bruised pain was increased by
pressure with the fingers (fifth day), 15 .—Aching distress in all the joints,
especially in the knees, ankles, and feet (first day), 4 *.—Severe aching dis¬
tress in the wrists, knees, ankles, and feet, all the afternoon (second day), 4 *.
—Dull aching distress in the hands, fingers, knees, and ankles (third
day), 4c .—In the afternoon, constant drawing pains in the wrists, knees, and
ankles, worse in the right knee and right wrist and fingers (first day), 45 .—
Drawing pains in the fingers and ankles, with distress in the right hypo-

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

197

chondrium and epigastric region (after six hours, fifth day); not so severe
(sixth day), 4 ''.—Drawing pains in the hands and ankles, at 5 p.m. (fourth
day), 4b .—Hard, dull, aching pains in the wrists, hands, fingers, and ankles

at 9 p.m. (first day), 0 .—Pain in shoulder, near the spine of right scapula,

ing pains through shoulder and chest (eighth day), 5 .—Transient rheumatic

Arm. [ 760 .] Rheumatic pains in arms (seventh day), 5 .—Had a few

biceps muscle, in the afternoon (fourth day ), 5 .—Elbotv and Forearm.
Drawing pain in the left elbow (after one hour and fifty-five minutes), 10 .—
—Several times through the day had drawing pains in right elbow-joint
and fingers (sixth day), 4a .—In the evening, while riding in cars, had a
severe pain in right forearm, lasting several minutes ; the pain seemed to
be in the flexor muscles of the forearm (tenth day), 11 .— Hands and,
Fingers. Nervous trembling of hands (third day), 6 .—Hands and fingers
ache constantly (third day), 4c .—Feeling in hands like that produced by
electricity (one hour and a half after fourth dose), 7a .—Prickling numbness
in hands ; sensation as if they were cold, and larger than usual (one hour
after fourth dose),A—[770.] Tingling in hands and fingers (four hours and
a half after fourth dose), 7 *.—Sensation of cold and numbness in hands;
they feel clumsy and stiff, with tingling and prickling; as if recovering
from cold (after three hours, second day), 7 .—Fine sharp pains in the fin¬
gers (second day), 4 *.—Frequent fine pains in the fingers and region of the
spleen (after eight hours), 41 .—While in bed in the evening, had fine prick¬
ling pains in the fingers (fifth day), 4 .

Inferior Extremities. —Weakness and depression all over the
body, especially in lower extremities, in the forenoon (fourth day), 6 .—
Feels a trembling and weariness in the lower limbs, at 10 a.m. (first day), 5 .—
Soreness and weariness in lower extremities, in the forenoon (third day), 8 .—
Aching in the lower extremities, with the general malaise (fourth day). 11 .—
Severe pain in the lower extremities, worse on standing (fifth day), 11 .—
Hip and Thigh. [780 ] Pain sometimes in the right hip (seventh and
teuth days),'° a .—Stitches in hip and shoulder, at 4 p.m. (first day), 5 . —
Throbbing pains in left hip, lasting only a few minutes, at 9 a.m. (seventh
day), 6a .—Severe, sharp, darting pains in the right thigh ; pains seem to be
muscular, and lasting for several minutes (second night), 11 .—Aching pains
in the back part of the thighs (fourth day), 11 .— Throbbing pains in gluteal
region (eighth day), 6 *.— Knees and Legs. Aching distress in the knees
and calves of the legs and small of the back (fifth day), 4 *.—Had very
severe aching distress in the right knee, all the evening (first day), 45 .—-
Rending pains around the left knee, which come and go rapidly (after four

198

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

hours and thirty-five minutes), 1 '.—Drawing pains in the knees and flexor
muscles (fifth day), 1 '.— [ 790 .] Sticking pain in left knee, at 9 p.m. (first
day), 0 .—Legs weak, during the forenoon (filth day), 1 '. Legs ached all day
(fourth day), 4 .—Aching distress in legs, back, and bowels, all the forenoon
(fourth day), 4a .—Legs and back ached, all the afternoon (sixth day), 4a .—
Legs ached, all the afternoon, until 7 p.m. (seventh day),'A—Aching dis¬
tress in the calves of both legs (first day), 4 '.—Severe pain in the left leg,
three inches below the knee (after two hours, second day), 11 .—Pains in the
right leg, below the knee, extending to the ankle (seventh day), 11 .—Ach¬
ing drawing pains in the left ankle, aggravated by motion; the pain ex¬
tends up the calf of the leg (after one hour and fifty-five minutes), 1 '.—
[ 800 .] Drawing pains in the left heel (after three hours), 4 *.

Generalities. —Restless and in pain, all over the head, stomach, and
bladder (after fourth dose, third day), 21 .—Arose feeling restless and uneasy
(fourth day), 3 .—Restless and uneasy; unable to sleep (first night), lc .—
Labor performed in a perfunctory manner (second day), 1 '.—Weakness,
with disinclination to move or study (fifth day), 11 .—Weakness of the whole
body (twenty-first day), 61 .—Weakness of the whole body ; the walls of the
chest especially feel as if they would sink in (ninth day), 61 .—A feeling of
weakness through the whole body (thirty-first day), 6a .—General feeling of
muscular weakness ; inclination to avoid all exertion, mental and muscu¬
lar ; sensation as if the nervous system were resting (half an hour after
fourth dose), 71 .— [ 810 .] Weak and irritable, all the forenoon, with the
frontal headache (fifth day), 1 '.—Felt weak in every limb, weak in brain,
weak in memory, thought, and will, as if a powerful and all-pervading dis¬
ease had fastened upon him (third day), 1 '.—Felt extremely weak, all day
(third day), 1 '.—Weariness, at 11 a.m. (fifth day), 2 .—Unusual fatigue after
slight exertion (first day), 2 .—Strong inclination to lie down and rest (third
day), 11 .—Some lassitude (second day), 2 .—Less energy than usual (tenth
day), 101 .—’Great lassitude and weariness throughout the afternoon (first
day), 2 . — Extreme lassitude (fourth day), 11 . — [ 820 .] Excessive languor,
with a feeling as if he had fever (after eight hours, fourth day), 41 ’.—Lan¬
guid feeling (first day), 4 '.—Awoke very languid (second day), 4c .—Languid
and feverish (after six hours, second day), 4c .—Languid, with dull feeling of
the head (after ten hours, second day), 4 '.—Languid (third day), 4 '.—Very
languid, from noon until 6, with a flushed face, and a feeling as if I had
fever (third day), 41 .—Feeling rather languid, at 9 p.m. (third day), 5 .—Felt
languid and lazy; had no inclination to stir; aversion to all muscular
exertion (one hour after second dose), 71 .—Languid all day (first and fifth
days), 41 .— [ 830 .] Very languid all the afternoon (second day), 4 *.—Great
languor, all the forenoon (fourth day), 41 .—During the afternoon, a sensa¬
tion of languor and weariness spreads over the whole system (third day), 2 .
—Very languid; energy entirely gone (fourth day), 2 .—Languid and dull,
with little inclination for either mental or physical exertion (after three
hours), 1 '. — Awoke at 7 A.M., languid and unrefreshed (third day), lb .—
Awoke languid and unrefreshed, and with the feeling of being mtentally
unequal to the business of the day (fourth day), lb —Languid and unre¬
freshed, on waking (second day), 1 .—In the morning, weak and languid
(second day), la .—A dull stupid feeling, all day (sixth day); a feeling of
dulness, aud inability to pursue studies (seventh day), 6 .— [ 840 .] General
feeling of malaise, with aching in the lower extremities, and premonitory
symptoms of fever (fourth day), 11 .—Usual feeling of malaise, on retiring
at 9 p.m. (fourth day), 2 .—Feeling of malaise (sixth day), 3 .—Malaise during

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

199

the afternoon (first day); general malaise (fourth and fifth days), 21 .—All
the afternoon felt a curious malaise, which prevented him from doing busi¬
ness with alacrity (third day), la . — Oppression (fourth day), 2 .—General
feeling of intoxication (half an hour after second dose, third day), 7 \—Sen¬
sation as if all objects were in violent agitation ; nothing seems to be at
rest (after second dose, third day), 7a .—Sick and faint, with a sudden shrink¬
ing from any mental work (soon), 10 .—Very sick indeed (after eight hours
and thirty-five minutes), 10 .— [ 850 .] Feel sick all over and indifferent to
duties, in the afternoon (fifth day), 3 .—A faint feeling on waking (seventh
morning), 3 . — Sick (after second dose), 7a .—Feeling very sick, at 7 p.m.
(third day), 21 .—General soreness of the body, on rising (seventh and tenth
mornings), 101 .—Arose feeling sore, tired, and sick, at 5 a.m. (third day), 2 *.
—Arose feeling sore, tired, and disgusted with everything (fourth morn¬
ing), 21 .—Head, back, knees, and calves of legs continued aching severely
all day, with rheumatic drawing pains in the elbows and bowels (fourth
day), 41 .—Rheumatic symptoms, for several days, 43 .—Nervous pain, alter¬
nating from the left arm to left eye and parietal region (soon), 2 .— [ 860 .]
Pains to-day worse on the right side (seventh day), 11 .—Felt much better
to-day till half past 4, when the pains of the extremities, back, and head
all returned (eighth day) ; pains in head, limbs, etc., not so severe (ninth
day), 11 .—Felt very badly all day (fifth day) ; better in the morning, but
in the afternoon felt quite badly again (sixth day), 11 .—Felt better in the
morning, but in the afternoon and evening much worse again (seventh
day), 11 .—No symptoms after supper (third day), 7 .—Symptoms aggravated
towards evening and on lying down ; ameliorated on motion and on ris¬
ing, 61 .— Right side principally affected ; symptoms more from right to left,
from above downwards, and from within outwards, 6 *.—Symptoms amelio¬
rated, towards evening (third day), 6 .—All the former symptoms, but greatly
ameliorated (tenth day), 6 .—All the symptoms ameliorated by a walk in
the open air (after one hour and three-quarters), 10 .— [ 870 .] All the symp¬
toms are bettter in the open air (second day), 10 .—All the symptoms have
declined to-day, especially the headache (seventh day), 10 .—All the symp¬
toms aggravated in a hot room and ameliorated in the cool air (first day), lb .
—All the symptoms are aggravated in the warm room and ameliorated in
the open air, though they are worse on commencing motion (sixth dav), lb .
—At supper ate some sour apple-sauce, when all the symptoms became
milder and gradually disappeared (seventh day), lb .—In the evening, ame¬
lioration of all the symptoms; though still languid and drowsy (third and
fourth days), 1 .—At 4 p.m., ate a bunch of somewhat tart grapes, and all
the symptoms disappeared; the nausea and headache were entirely removed
in a few minutes (first day), 1 *.

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
, —During the last three or four days there was a peculiar reddish-
clouded appearance of the skin over the whole body, which disappeared
two days after discontinuing the drug, 10 .—Skin dry and parched (third
evening), 21 .—Eruption under the right ear, discharging a watery fluid (fifth
day), 61 .— [ 880 .] Right ear inflamed and somewhat swollen (twelfth day);
right ear broke out in white blisters on red base; copious discharge of a
watery fluid on puncturing; shooting pains in ear when lying on that side
(thirteenth day); vesicles on ear dried up and cuticle desquamating; ach¬
ing in outer edge of ear when lying down, relieved by pressure (fifteenth
day), 6 .—In evening, intense itching of right ear (twenty-fifth day); ear
swollen, little white vesicles rising under epidermis (twenty-sixth day) ;
swelling of ear increasing (twenty-seventh day); the white vesicles in ear

200

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

assumed a purple tinge (twenty-eighth day) ; ear not so much swollen
(twenty-ninth day) ; desquamation of cuticle of right ear; the blisters dis¬
charged water (thirtieth day); stinging pains in right ear; great soreness
of the ear during the day; the blisters on the ear scab over, and become
filled with a greenish-looking pus, at 5 p.m. ; pains in ear of intense throb¬
bing nature, worse on moving and exposure to the air; when walking,
wants to hold his hand over it; sometimes pains shoot from it to the boil
on forehead (thirty-second day); face swollen in front of right ear and
painful to the touch ; the ear is not painful to-day; some pus is discharged,
and the scabs desquamate (thirty-third day); ear healing up (thirty-eighth
day), 6 \—A boil began to make its appearance on right side of forehead
(the first in his life), (twenty-sixth day); it discharges some pus every day
(thirty-eighth day); it discharged no more (after forty-five days), and by
the forty-eighth day it had entirely disappeared. About the same time,
another one made its appearance on right side of the chin, which continued
painful until the fifty-third day, when it discharged some purulent matter,
and then began to pass off; by the fifty-sixth day it was all gone, and from
that date he experienced no symptoms/ 5 .—Red spots on lower extremities,
alike in position on both ; after an hour or so, they would change to a
purple color; there would be no itching quite near or on the spots, but
around on the healthy skin ; itching not so annoying while perspiring
(fourth day). An hour before breakfast counted as many as fifty spots on
various parts of the body, most of them on upper and lower extremities,
one or two on the chest; itching more confined to the trunk (fifth day).
Discontinued the use of the drug for two weeks, during which time the
itching continued as annoying as ever; by getting in the least degree ex¬
cited or warmed, the spots would be as red as ever, but in an hour or so
would subside and assume a purple hue; after the expiration of two weeks
could see where the spots had been ; the itching was as annoying as ever;
it did not produce any disorganization of the skin ; as the spots disappeared
they became of a dirty-yellow color, somewhat like that left by a bruise, 8 .
—A slight bruise on the large joint of little finger of right hand inflames
and suppurates, causing painful tension of the fingers of that hand (thirty-
fifth day) ; vesicular eruption on right hand, commencing at the sore on
little finger and gradually extending upwards (thirty-ninth day); the
eruption appears under right ear, and gradually extends over the whole
face and neck and on right hip; burning and itching sensation in the
eruptions; ou scratching they discharge water (fortieth day); burning in
eruptions, increased on exposure to air; much worse to-day than yesterday
(forty-first day) ; no more burning or itching; the eruptions began to dis¬
appear (forty-second day); all gone, and desquamation of the cuticle set
in (forty-fifth day), 6 \—A lame spot on inside of right knee, as large as a
penny, on waking from afternoon nap (fifth day); still felt (sixth morn¬
ing), 5 .—It occasioned quite an irritation of the skin. The itching was so
intense all over the body that she could not be induced to continue the
proving longer. She described it as so many thousand fleas on her; could
not refrain from constant scratching; the itching was not worse at night, 9 .
—Itching of the right ear, at 6 p.m. (eleventh day), 6 .—Intense itching on
back of right hand (thirteenth day), 61 .—A prickling in lower extremities,
almost like that of pins, mostly in popliteal space; on scratching, it burns
like fire, but no change in color of the skin (after second dose, third day);
burning in the skin of lower extremities, like fire; could get more relief
from rubbing than scratching (third night), 8 .

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Sleepiness. [ 890 .] Constant inclination to yawn (after
eight hours, fourth day), 4b .—A 3 p.m. drowsiness succeeded pain in umbili¬
cal region, and the slightest effort, seemed to weary (seventh day), 2 .—Drow¬
siness, in the afternoon (sixth day), 11 .—Drowsiness (one hour after third
dose), 11 .—Extraordinary inclination to sleep (sixth day), 1 .—Sudden sleepi¬
ness (after thirty-five minutes), 1 '.—Ten hours of sound refreshing sleep
(fifth night) ; slept ten hours (sixth night), 5 .—Sleepiness excessive; went
to bed at 8 p.m. (sixth day), 1 .—Slept soundly all night (second, third, and
fourth nights); retired at 8, and slept soundly all night (fifth night); went
to bed early, and slept soundly all night (sixth night) ; after a walk, lay
down and slept three hours, in the afternoon (eighth dav), 5a .—Sound sleep
all night, but haunted by frightful dreams (third and fourth days), 1 .—
[ 900 .] During the night heavy sleep, with less vivid dreams than on the
previous night (second day),' 1 .—Sleep heavy, and troubled with dreams of
robbers, etc. (third night), 11 .—Sleep from 5 a.m. to 7 a.m. ; languid and
tired on awaking (fifth day), 1 .— Sleeplessness and Dreams. Awoke
about 2 a.m. with severe pains in forehead, roaring in the ears, and very
severe pain in right kidney; very restless and uneasy, rolling and tossing
about; could not get to sleep for a long time from pain and restlessnes; in
the morning felt some better; pain in kidney relieved (tenth day), 11 .—
Restless night, full of dreams, with some fever (seventh night), 5 .—Restless
and tossing, and some difficulty in falling asleep (first day), 11 .—Sleep rest¬
less and uneasy, awaking unrefreshed and languid (ninth night), 1 .—Rest¬
less night (second night), 2 *.—Rolled around till after midnight, when sleep
gave some intermission to the constant pain (third day), 2a .—Awoke at 7
a.m. tired and unrefreshed, after one and a half hours’ sleep (second day), 1 '.
— [ 910 .] Sleep unusually deep and heavy (first night); sleep broken and
restless, and at waking intervals hardly able to determine whether sleeping
or waking (second night), u ’.—The sleep during the night was heavy, but
restless, with fantastic dreams, practicing medicine among people of gigan¬
tic stature; suddenly the scene would change, and his patients were about
the size of peas (third night), 11 .—Sleep heavy and dream-haunted (fourth
night), 11 .—Sleep uneasy and unrefreshing, and with more annoying dreams
than before (sixth night), 11 .—Restless sleep (first night), 1 .—At a quarter
past nine, on awaking, was attacked with a kind of nightmare; quite con¬
scious, but unable to stir on account of a pressing weight in the stomach
and whole front of the trunk (sixth day), 1 .—Dreamed of armies of soldiers
rising out of their graves and marching into the house (third night);
dreamed of enemies prowling about the house (fourth night), 10a .—Awoke
during night with nightmare (third night), 3 .—Sleep disturbed by dreams
(fifth night), 2 ; (third night), 3 .—Sleep dream-haunted (third night), 1 '.—
[ 920 .] One long and remarkably vivid dream all night till four (fifth
night), 1 '.—Unpleasant dreams during the whole night (first night) ; sleep
broken by dreams, at first of a frightful nature, but towards morning las¬
civious (third night), lh .—The dreams during the night were so vivid and
lifelike as to seem, on waking, as if he had been up all night (first night), 11 .
—Slept well until 2 a.m., when he awoke, dreaming of fighting (first night);
most frightful dreams; dreamed of getting whipped and killing snakes
(second night); dreamed as before (third night); could go to sleep quite
easily; was able to sleep only a short time, awaking from horrible dreams,
and covered with a profuse perspiration (fourth night), 8 .—Dreamed of dead
animals (second night), 01 .—Had dreams of food, and awoke hungry (third
night); slept pretty well, but had some dreams of food (fourth night), 5 .

202

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chilliness. Chilliness and shivering over the whole body;
could not keep warm, even by sitting over the stove (soon), 1 '.—Shivering
in a warm room, and the head hot (after forty-five minutes), 1 ®.—Shivering
from the hips downwards (after forty-five minutes), 1 '.—Shivering, with
chattering of the teeth ; scarcely comfortable near a large fire (after one
hour and ten minutes), 1 '.— [ 930 .] Chilliness and shivering accompanied
passage from bowels (after two hours and thirty-five minutes), 1 ®.—Shud¬
dering and horripilation (after three hours and twenty minutes), 1 '.—Dur¬
ing the stool, shuddering, with chilliness of the sacral region (second day), 1 '.
—Chilliness, with great sensitiveness to cold air, and desire to be near the
fire (fourth day); chilliness, and extreme sensitiveness to cold air (fifth
day), 11 .—At times cold streaks run up and down the spine (twenty-first
day), 61 .—Frequent shuddering sensations, 13 .— Heat,. Feverish (half an
hour after fourth dose), 2 .—On awaking, fever (second day), 2 .—Somewhat
feverish (eighth day); feverish (ninth day), 2 .—Flushes of heat, alternating
with chilliness, all through the day (first day), 1 .— [ 940 .] Feverish heat,
lasting all day, accompanied by pains in all the limbs, and nausea (second
day), 1 .—Felt feverish, irritable, and intolerant of noise (fourth day), la .—•
Hot and feverish all day (twelfth day 1 ), 1 .—Awoke towards morning feeling
somewhat feverish (fourth night), 5 .—Hot flushes and slight headache, at 2
p.m. (seventh day), 3 .—Some fever (seventh night), 5 .—Dry heat over the
whole body, especially on the palms of the hands (first night), 1 '.—Dry heat
over the body, with sweat on the forehead (third day), 1 '.—Dry heat, most
on the parts where the pain is worst (sixth day), lb .—Hot, dry feeling over
the whole body, with a sensation as of having slept without undressing, or
having sat up all night (fifth day), 15 .— [ 950 .] Dry heat over the whole
body, especially in the palms of the hands (fourth day),’\—Awoke with
dry heat over the whole body, especially on the face and hands (sixth
night), 1 *.—The dry heat over the body continues, though the feet are cold
(seventh day), 13 .—After dinner, heat of skin and profuse perspiration, with
increased nausea (third and fourth days), 1 .—Heat of skin, at 4 p.m. (fifth
day), 1 .—Head hot and feverish, with dull aching in the frontal region,
especially on moving the eyes (first night), 1 '.—Heat of the face and head,
with racking frontal headache (after ten hours and a half, fifth day), lb .—
Burning cheeks and hot flushes, with pulse at 96, at 2 p.m. (eighth day), 5 .
—Feeling feverish ; hands hot and dry, and ache constantly (after nine
hours), 4 '.—Hands hot and dry (after six hours), 4 '.— [ 960 .] In the morn¬
ing, hands and feet hot and feverish (second day), 1 ®.— Sweat. Profuse
perspiration on waking; felt all the afternoon as if he would break out
into profuse perspiration, but did not (fourth day), 8 .—Sweat all night
(twenty-second night), 6 *.—Passage accompanied by sweat on the forehead
and head, though the morning was cool (first day), 1 .—Sweat on forehead,
accompanying the rumbling and swelling in the umbilical region (after six
hours), 15 .—Sweat on the forehead, with the rising of the bitter fluid (fifth
day), 1 .

Conditions. —Aggravation.— ( Toward morning'), Gastric and hepatic
symptoms.— (Morning), After eating, liveliness, followed by depression ; on
rising, headache; throbbing headache; on awaking, headache; before rising,
headache through cerebrum ; shooting pains in head ; on rising, pressure
in frontal region and in root of nose; on waking, frontal headache; 6 a.m.,
headache in frontal and temporal regions; pain in right temple; ringing
in the ears; everything tastes and smells sour; on waking, unable to speak
aloud; before rising, pricking pains in throat; 6 am., hunger; craving

PTELEA TRIFOLIATA.

203

for acid food; on rising, pain in right hypochondrium; pain in the bowels;
8.40 a.m., urging to stool; 6 a.m. till 3 P.M., urging to stool; 6 A.M., on
awaking, desire to urinate ; on awaking, sexual desire ; before rising, sen¬
sation as of a foreign substance in larynx; backache; on awaking, pain in
small of back ; pain in lumbar region ; lameness in region of kidneys ;
sharp pain in arms; on awaking, faint feeling; on rising, soreness of the
body ; hands and feet hot and feverish ; on awaking, perspiration.— (Fore¬
noon), Lowness of spirits; 11 a.m., unsteadiness and nervous irritability;
headache; 11 a.m., frontal headache, lasting ten minutes; pressive feeling
in forehead; frontal headache; pressive pain from temple to temple; cut¬
ting pains in right temple; 9 a.m., pain behind right ear; 8 a m., pain in
left ear; 10 a.m., feeling as if tongue were cut in middle and were just
healing up; 9 to 11 a.m., nausea; 11 a.m., oppression at epigastrium; 9
a.m., pain in epigastrium ; pains in hypochondriac regions ; distress in re¬
gion of spleen and right side of umbilicus; 11.35 a.m., pain in spleen;
di stress in bowels, back, and legs; 10 a.m., pain in bowels; pain under
right breast; neck stiff; weakness and depression all over body; 10 a.m.,
trembling and weariness in lower limbs; soreness and weariness in lower
extremities; legs weak.— (Noon), Headache in left temple; pain in right
mastoid process of temporal bone ; neck feels swollen ; pain in back of

( Afternoon ), Anxiety, with headache; dulness; 5 p.m., giddiness,

8 p.m. , aching of right molar teeth; sore throat; unpleasant feeling in
throat; 1.30 p.m., constriction of pharynx; 4 p.m., sour rising from stom¬
ach ; 3 p.m., hiccough; nausea; pain in epigastric and umbilical regions;

ral regions; aching in the limbs; distress in wrists, knees, ankles, and feet;

2 p.m., transient rheumatic pains in right side and right shoulder-blade;

ache in left zygomatic region; 10 p.m., headache in temporal region; pain
in left side of head ; pain in head ; after going to bed, pain over eyes;
pain behind right ear; roaring in the ears; 7 p.m., lower molar teeth ache;
aching of right molar teeth ; teeth sensitive and painful; 8 p.m., throat
sore; 9 p.m., constriction of pharynx; nausea; 9.30 p.m., nausea and rum¬
bling in bowels; 9 p.m., unpleasant sensation in stomach ; distress in right
hypochondrium ; uneasiness in umbilical region ; 8 p.m., pain in umbilical

region ; after going to bed, colicky pains in umbilical region ; pain and
rumbling in bowels; colicky pains in small intestines; 9 p.m., in bed, sharp
pain across abdomen; before stool, colicky pains in hypogastrium ; 7 p.m.,
tenesmus; urging to stool ; throbbing pain from glans penis to left pubic
region; when breathing, walls of chest feel as if they had not the power to
expand ; pain in lower part of lung; 9 p.m., pain in back of left breast; 7
p.m., backache; pain in left shoulder-blade; while riding in cars, pain in
right forearm ; in bed, prickling pains in fingers; aching distress in right
knee; 9 p.m., sticking pain in left knee; on retiring, feeling of malaise ; 7
p.m., sick feeling.— (Night), 1 to 5 a.m., mind wandering; when retiring at
10.30, head confused and giddy; 11 p.m., sudden attack of vertigo; frontal
headache; 12.45 p.m., shooting paiu through temple, with headache and
nausea; 11.15 p.m., dryness of mouth ; 1 a.m., rising of bitter fluid; heart¬
burn, with sensation of agitation of all the muscles; weight in stomach ; 1
a.m., awakened by pressing pain in stomach ; 10 p.m., pain in right hypo¬
chondriac region; 1 a.m., awoke with pain in abdomen; pain in bowels;
pressure in rectum; wheu lying on back, pressure on the lungs; pain in
back; restless, with dreaming; sweat.— (Open air), Pain in ear; burning

Feels sick all over. Lack of reaction, in chronic diseases. After-effects of infectious diseases,
lasting for years. Enfeebled. RECURRENCE. Clears up confused cases. Migraine. Quinsy.
FOUL; discharges; stools; eruptions; sweat; stubborn footsweat; odor of body. Thick
secretions. Weak, tender and thin, easily chilled; takes cold; clothing seems large or he feels
pushed down. Joints seem loose. HUNGRY or unusually well BEFORE AN ATTACK; but
debilitated and reacts badly, and chronicity threatens. Wants to wash parts. ....................
ANXIETY. Forebodings. Despair, of recovery. Gloomy. Feels good and bad by turns. Horrid
thoughts. Averse to work. Feels himself poor (reverse-Sul.). Mind dull, clouded, difficult
thinking. Head feels separated from body. Headache, follows visual disturbances; alternates
with other troubles. Twitching in temples. Sensitive to drafts about head; wants it covered, in
hot water. Dull, dry, tangled hair. Gummy, everted eyelids. Humid sores behing ears. Putrid
otorrheea. Hay fever. Face pale, sickly, dirty, fuzzy or puffy. Loose teeth. Tip of tongue feels
burnt (Ign.). Hawks out foul, cheesy masses. Filthy taste. Anorexia; with great thirst. Flatus like
bad eggs. DARK, GUSHING, HORRIBLY PUTRID STOOLS; of penetrating odor, going
through whole house (Pod.); < at night. Cholera infantum. Stool soft, but difficult. Bed-wetting;
at full moon. Offensive genitals. Griping in testes. Chronic gonorrhea. Breathes > lying down or
spreading arms apart. Breathing; < open air. Cough, < lying. Gurgling at heart. Panaris. Lumbar
ache, < standing or walking. Hot, itching soles. Skin breaks out; < flexures; is dirty, rough or
scabby, greasy. Condylomata, on edges of skin. Intolerable itching; < heat (of bed); he

scratches it raw or until it bleeds. Heat, with steaming sweat. Sweat; profuse; < night; on palms;
cold; easy.
